text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan shelves a planned visit to Libya to avoid a crisis in his coalition with a pro-Western party.
- Famous Turkish classical music singer Zeki Muren's tapes and CDs sold out three days after his death this week.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller tells former U.S. assistant secretary of state Richard Holbrooke that she regrets having gone into a coalition with the Islamists.
- Ciller asks International Monetary Fund (IMF) to back harsh economic austerity measures.
- Money previously spent on gambling now flows to stock exchange as government tries to ban Turks from casinos.
- Some 38 women's organisations make joint statement against Islamist activities.
- Foreign investors in Istanbul stock exchange will be required to declare their identities as of October 7.
- Police special forces and state-paid village guards confess to string of crimes in mainly-Kurdish southeast Turkey.
- Medicine price rises arbitrary in Turkey.
